facts.statement: Zhuchengtyrannus lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in Shandong Province, China.
facts.quote: known from the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous of Shandong Province, China

facts.statement: Zhuchengtyrannus was first described and named by David W. E. Hone and colleagues in 2011.
facts.quote: Zhuchengtyrannus was first described and named by David W. E. Hone, Kebai Wang, Corwin Sullivan, Xijin Zhao, Shuqing Chen, Dunjin Li, Shuan Ji, Qiang Ji and Xing Xu in 2011

facts.statement: The holotype was collected from the Zangjiazhuang quarry in Zhucheng City, dating to at least 73.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: ZCDM V0031 was collected in the Hongtuya Formation from the Wangshi Group at Zangjiazhuang quarry, Zhucheng City, dating to the Campanian stage, at least 73.5 million years ago

facts.statement: Zhuchengtyrannus was a large carnivorous theropod estimated to be about 10 meters in body length and 5 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: Zhuchengtyrannus was a large carnivorous theropod, and the holotype has been estimated to have been "similar in size and gross morphology to Tarbosaurus", which is about 10 m in body length and 5 MT in body mass

facts.statement: A 2013 phylogenetic analysis recovered Zhuchengtyrannus as the sister taxon of Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis published with the description of the tyrannosaurine Lythronax in the journal PLOS One by Loewen et al. 2013, recovered Zhuchengtyrannus as the sister taxon of Tarbosaurus

facts.statement: Research suggests Zhuchengtyrannus and other Asian tyrannosaurids descended from a North American stem lineage that later gave rise to Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: It also suggests that Zhuchengtyrannus and other currently known Asian tyrannosaurids were part of an evolutionary radiation descending from the same North American stem that later gave rise to Tyrannosaurus rex

facts.statement: A 2024 study found Zhuchengtyrannus to be the closest relative of Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: A 2024 study by Dalman and colleagues, incorporating their new species Tyrannosaurus mcraeensis instead found Zhuchengtyrannus to be the closest relative of Tarbosaurus

facts.statement: Zhuchengtyrannus lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, approximately between 83.5 million years ago during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a fines del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 83.5 million years ago durante el Campaniense y Maastrichtiense

facts.statement: Zhuchengtyrannus is one of the largest known carnivorous theropods, with the holotype estimated to be between 10 and 12 meters in length.
facts.quote: Es uno de los mayores terópodos carnívoros conocidos, y se estima que el holotipo medía entre 10 a 12 metros de longitud

facts.statement: It is debated whether isolated teeth from the 1970s named Tyrannosaurus zhuchengensis belong to Zhuchengtyrannus or a related species.
facts.quote: It is possible that several isolated teeth recovered from one of the Zhucheng dinosaur quarries during the 1970s, previously given the name Tyrannosaurus zhuchengensis, belong to this or a related species

facts.statement: Isolated teeth previously named Tyrannosaurus zhuchengensis may belong to Zhuchengtyrannus magnus or a closely related species.
facts.quote: Es posible que varios dientes aislados de una de las canteras de dinosaurios de Zhucheng, a los que anteriormente se les dio el nombre de Tyrannosaurus zhuchengensis, pertenecen a esta especie o una muy relacionada.

facts.statement: The teeth of the related species T. zhuchengensis feature serrated edges extending from the base to the crown, a trait not seen in any other tyrannosaurine.
facts.quote: Los dientes de T. zhuchengensis se caracterizan por bordes aserrados que se extienden a lo largo de la base a la corona dental, una característica no vista en ninguna otra especie de tiranosaurino.

facts.statement: Discoverers described Zhuchengtyrannus magnus as a tyrannosaurine but did not perform a phylogenetic analysis due to scarce material.
facts.quote: Zhuchengtyrannus magnus fue descrito como un tiranosaurino por sus descubridores, pero debido al escaso material no realizaron un análisis filogenético

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis published alongside Lythronax argestes found that Zhuchengtyrannus magnus is the sister taxon of T. bataar.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético publicado con la descripción del tiranosaurino Lythronax argestes en la publicación PLOS ONE encontró que Zhuchengtyrannus magnus es el taxón hermano de T. bataar.

facts.statement: A 2016 study by Stephen Brusatte and Thomas Carr placed Z. magnus as the sister taxon to the clade containing Tarbosaurus bataar and Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un estudio filogenético de los tiranosáuridos realizada por los paleontólogos Stephen Brusatte y Thomas Carr en 2016 coloca a Z. magnus como taxón hermano del clado conformado por Tarbosaurus bataar y Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: Z. magnus was found in the Zangjiazhuang quarry, a Cretaceous floodplain containing one of the highest concentrations of dinosaur bones in the world.
facts.quote: Z. magnus fue encontrado en la cantera Zangjiazhuang, una área que fue una planicie inundable en el período Cretácico y que contiene una de las más altas concentraciones de huesos de dinosaurios en el mundo.

facts.statement: Alongside tyrannosaurid material, the quarry yielded specimens of Sinoceratops, hadrosaurs, likely Shantungosaurus, and indeterminate ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: Aparte del material de tiranosáurido, en la cantera se han recuperado especímenes de Sinoceratops, hadrosáuridos. probablemente Shantungosaurus y anquilosaurios indeterminados.

facts.statement: Zhuchengtyrannus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Zhuchengtyrannus belongs to the parent group Tyrannosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tyrannosaurini

facts.statement: Zhuchengtyrannus is classified in the family Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Tyrannosauridae
